facts.fact: ANPTIC, the national ICT promotion agency, with the World Bank and the Open Data Institute launched the Burkina Open Data Initiative (BODI), a single platform for publishing non-sensitive administration data, on 5 June 2014; the document describes data.gov.bf as the portal.
A civil society member said more than 200 datasets had been published on the open data portal in 2016, though most documents were PDFs rather than reusable CSV or Excel.

The BODI section of the ANPTIC website links to four reusable data applications, an open data platform and an open election platform; the document is dated 2019 (published date, inferred) and gives no date for the applications.

note: OGP commitment BF0011 targets 500 datasets by June 2019 (a plan, not a fact); no open licence and no list of several publishing bodies is stated.

facts.fact: The government says its portal data.gov.bf, set up with World Bank support, holds 261 datasets on education, health, ICT and agriculture.

The government says four applications have been developed that reuse the data.gov.bf datasets, and that the BODI initiative led by ANPTIC produced Open Election and the NENDO school-data map on open data.

facts.fact: leFaso.net reports INSD presented the Burkina open data platform, set up in 2016 with African Development Bank funding, where data is available in machine-readable Excel format.
leFaso.net reports the Burkina open data platform brings together in one place the statistical outputs of the different ministries, with data on health, education and household living standards.
INSD, the national statistics institute, says it held a session on disseminating indicators on the open data portal (ODP) at burkinafaso.opendataforafrica.org, with sector ministry staff taking part.
INSD says a working session updated the Open Data Platform of Burkina (ODP) to make all data of the 2022 national statistical yearbook available, in reusable formats such as Word and Excel.
